summary: An intermediate course on Q-learning covering foundational concepts, value iteration algorithms, and practical implementation considerations.

modules.title: Markov Decision Processes and Bellman Equations
modules.query: Markov decision process MDP Bellman equation value function optimal policy
learning_goals: Explain how Markov decision processes formalize sequential decision-making problems
Derive and apply the Bellman equation to compute value functions
Understand the relationship between value functions and optimal policies

modules.title: Dynamic Programming and Value Iteration
modules.query: dynamic programming value iteration temporal difference learning control
learning_goals: Distinguish between policy iteration and value iteration algorithms
Implement value iteration to solve finite MDPs
Understand how dynamic programming approximates optimal value functions

modules.title: Q-Learning Algorithm and Convergence
modules.query: Q-learning off-policy temporal difference control algorithm convergence properties
learning_goals: Explain the Q-learning update rule and how it differs from SARSA
Understand why Q-learning is an off-policy algorithm
Analyze convergence conditions and learning rate effects on Q-learning performance

modules.title: Function Approximation and Practical Implementation
modules.query: Q-learning function approximation neural networks deep Q-learning convergence
learning_goals: Apply function approximation techniques to handle large state spaces
Implement Q-learning with linear and nonlinear function approximators
Identify and mitigate stability issues in practical Q-learning applications
